issues.failure_explanation: The step $\sum_{i\in O}p_i(w_{SM})\le\epsilon^k$ (which yields $m\|w_{SM}-w^*\|\le\epsilon^kG$) is valid only when the outliers are exactly the $|\mathbb O|$ highest-loss samples at $w_{SM}$, in which case $\sum_{i\in O}p_i=\frac{|\mathbb O|^k}{n^k}=\epsilon^k$ via the with-replacement probabilities of eq:probability; without that ordering the sum can be as large as $1-(1-\epsilon)^k$. The lemma, however, is stated for 'any first order stationary point' and never assumes the ball condition. In addition the bound is stated with $\lambda:=\min_w\lambda_w$ from eq:lambdasc, whose positivity in the outlier setting is never established (at spurious stationary points $\langle\nabla\tilde F(w),w-w^*\rangle=0$, forcing $\lambda_w\le0$); the proof actually delivers the good-sample parameter $m(w_{SM})>0$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the lemma to stationary points in $\mathcal B_r(w^*)$ (the hypothesis the theorem already assumes) and replace $\lambda$ by the good-set secant parameter $m\ge p_{\min}\lambda_{good}$; a limited weakening that leaves the theorem's chain intact.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma as stated is unproved for arbitrary stationary points; Theorem theorem:relativebounds invokes it under the extra hypothesis $w_{SM}\in\mathcal B_r(w^*)$ (which repairs the $\epsilon^k$ step) but inherits the unestablished positivity of $\lambda$ in the outlier setting.

issues.why_classification: A contained repair (add the ball hypothesis, use the good-set parameter) restores a recognizably comparable result with no new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof replaces the without-replacement coefficients $\frac{2(n-i)}{n(n-1)}$ on outlier ranks $i=|\mathcal G|+1,\dots,n$ by $\frac1n$. Since $\frac{2(n-i)}{n(n-1)}\le\frac1n$ holds only for ranks $i\ge(n+1)/2$, and the gradient terms are nonnegative, the replacement is not an upper bound for ranks $i<(n+1)/2$ — which exist throughout the corollary's regime $|\mathcal G|\le n/2$ whenever $|\mathcal G|<(n-1)/2$. Hence '$R_t^{(MKL_2)}\le R_t^{(SGD)}$ if (eq:get) holds' is unjustified, and the conclusion can fail: if the outlier gradient mass at $w_t$ concentrates on the lowest-loss outlier (rank $|\mathcal G|+1$) and eq:get is tight, MKL's outlier term is up to about twice SGD's and the comparison reverses while all hypotheses hold. (The corollary also silently switches to without-replacement probabilities although the paper announced a with-replacement focus.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No source-supported repair: the per-term comparison is invalid precisely in the advertised regime; saving the result requires excluding it (e.g. $|\mathcal G|\ge(n-1)/2$) or a new argument controlling outlier gradients, so the comparison as stated is abandoned.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix's claim that MKL-2 always dominates SGD in one-step expected distance even when corruptions exceed half is false as stated in its advertised regime; the main-text sentence advertising this sufficient condition loses its support.
issues.title: Corollary cor:added-1's comparison R_t^(MKL_2) <= R_t^(SGD) uses an invalid per-term coefficient replacement in exactly its advertised regime
issues.why_classification: The proof's key inequality is false in the corollary's advertised regime and the conclusion can fail; every repair excludes the advertised regime or needs a new argument — a major loss for this result.
